summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 31% to INR1,630 crore and Q4 revenue grew 42% to INR447.8 crore; management guides to 20%+ volume growth in FY27.
summary.overview: Innova Captab reported its highest-ever annual performance, with FY26 consolidated revenue of INR1,630 crore (+31% YoY) and Q4 revenue of INR447.8 crore (+42% YoY). Growth was led by the CDMO business (INR1,133 crore, +24% for FY26) and Branded Generics (INR497 crore, +51%), with the Jammu facility's first full year of ramp-up a major contributor. FY26 EBITDA rose to INR250.3 crore (15.4% margin) from INR198.2 crore, while PAT grew 10% to INR140.9 crore. Management said Jammu is near EBITDA breakeven and expects it to turn EBITDA-positive in the coming quarter.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,133 crore (+24%); Q4 INR314.8 crore (+41%). Customer base above 350 clients, including several leading Indian pharma companies. Baddi facility grew about 35% YoY, mainly on volumes.

segments.name: Branded Generics
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR497 crore (+51%); Q4 INR133 crore (+46%). Domestic is trade generics, roughly 70% domestic and 30-35% exports per management; not tracked by geography at segment level.

segments.name: Jammu facility
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR300 crore revenue in FY26; Q4 exit run rate above INR90 crore. Management says EBITDA is near breakeven and expects EBITDA-positive in the next quarter.

segments.name: Sharon Bio
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR240 crore; export regulated markets (Canada, UK, Europe, Australia); margin above company average per management.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of 20%+ revenue growth, and said volume growth of 20%+ at group level is maintained for FY27 from FY26.

EBITDA growth expected to outpace revenue growth as Jammu utilisation ramps up; PAT growth expected to outpace EBITDA growth because Jammu depreciation and finance costs are largely fixed and already in the base.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to be better than FY26 (15.4%); management cited a few percentage points of improvement from operating leverage, without quantifying.
Proposed new Baddi general block: capex INR150-170 crore, spent across FY27 and FY28; optimum revenue potential INR450-500 crore. Still under deliberation.
Greenfield projects take about 1.5 years to reach commercial production, so new-plant depreciation and interest are expected to hit P&L mainly from FY28.
capex_capacity: Jammu facility completed its first full year of operation in FY26; ramp-up progressing steadily. Jammu houses injectables, general, cephalosporin, beta-lactam and penems; new formats include BFS and respules.

Baddi land parcel (about INR20-odd crore, disclosed earlier) acquired for a general oral tablet, capsule and oral liquid block to relieve high utilisation at Baddi; detailed note to follow once finalised.
Maintenance capex continues at recent percentage-of-revenue trend; new Baddi block capex of INR150-170 crore expected across FY27 and FY28.
Regulatory milestones: Baddi cephalosporin facility received UK-MHRA approval; Jammu blocks received PIC/S certification via SMDC Ukraine. Company also cites EU-GMP certification.
demand_pricing: Cephalosporin API prices fell in Q2 and Q3 FY26, stabilised in early Q4, and rose on a YTD basis into April 2026 amid the Middle East conflict; management said Q4 itself saw no meaningful sequential rise.

CDMO pricing is cost-plus, and management said raw-material increases have largely been passed through to customers. Management said raw-material availability is not a concern; the issue is price, not supply.
Gross margin decline YoY attributed solely to product mix; management said raw-material price increases had no impact on gross margin.
Management said the Jammu revenue contribution is being used to both CDMO and Branded Generics; split not disclosed.
Management did not give a split of CDMO growth between volume and realisation at group level.

qa_highlights.question: Split of CDMO growth between volume and realisation for FY26 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not track volume at entity level; Baddi grew about 35% YoY, mainly on volumes, with Jammu ramp-up a key driver.

qa_highlights.question: Is Jammu EBITDA positive, and how close to breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Jammu did about INR300 crore in FY26 and is nearing EBITDA breakeven in Q4; management expects EBITDA-positive and fixed-cost coverage in the coming quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall YoY despite a higher branded share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline only to product mix; raw-material price increases had no impact on gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: Ex-Jammu EBITDA margin of about 18%? Is it a good estimate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed with the analyst's back-of-envelope calculation of about 18.2% ex-Jammu EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for Baddi land purchase and FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Baddi general block is for higher-utilisation general portfolio; capex INR150-170 crore spread across FY27 and FY28, with optimum revenue INR450-500 crore; still under deliberation.

qa_highlights.question: Sharon Bio revenue and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Sharon revenue about INR240 crore in FY26, with a margin above the company average given its export regulatory market focus.

risks_watch: Management declined to give a split of CDMO and Branded Generics revenue for Jammu, and of CDMO growth between domestic and export; limits visibility on segment mix.
Raw-material and API price volatility from the Middle East conflict; cost-plus pass-through is assumed but timing lag is not quantified.
Jammu EBITDA breakeven timing and utilisation ramp; the company guided that it will turn positive next quarter.
Baddi block project (capex INR150-170 crore) is still under deliberation; timing and scope not finalised.
Management declined to quantify FY27 margin expansion, saying it depends on product mix and geography.
Semaglutide: management is not targeting first-launch; plans a later-wave entry depending on market and exhibit batch filings.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and capacity, with the 20%+ FY27 volume guidance restated more than once. Evasive on segment and facility-level splits (Jammu, CDMO volume versus price, domestic versus export), and cautious on quantifying FY27 margin expansion.
key_quotes: FY '26 has been a defining year for Innova Captab as we achieved our highest ever annual performance, reflecting the strength of our business model, execution capabilities and customer relationship.
So whatever the incremental revenue will come, it will trigger the operational leverage, and we expect that there should be a few percent point improvement in the EBITDA.

And in coming quarter, as we said that the Jammu ramp-up is going on. We are very much positive that in coming quarter, we should be able to achieve EBITDA positive as well as start covering the fixed cost on Jammu part.

financial_highlights.value: 31% of FY26 revenue; 28% of Q4 revenue

adds.what: Proposed new Baddi general oral tablet, capsule and oral liquid block (INR150-170 cr capex; optimum revenue potential INR450-500 cr)

growth.why: Management guides 20%+ revenue and volume growth for FY27 (reiterated from FY26 base) and a few-point EBITDA margin improvement over FY26's 15.4%, backed by Jammu ramp-up toward EBITDA breakeven and a proposed Baddi block (INR150-170 cr, FY27-FY28) that is still under deliberation, so backing is partial rather than contracted.
